description: Curated external project references, not vendored code or installed dependencies. Inspect upstream afresh before using.

entries.name: Hallmark
entries.use_when: Building or reviewing distinctive landing pages, web UI and visual systems; avoiding generic AI-looking layouts and checking responsive quality.
look_for: Distinctive visual directions and theme selection rather than generic templates
Real browser-based visual checks, accessibility/contrast and responsive layouts
Audit/redesign workflow and preservation of existing functional behavior
cautions: Its upstream install or invocation does not happen just because it is indexed here.
Theme count, rules and implementation can change; consult the live upstream skill before relying on details.
Design rules are inspiration, not a license to copy assets or make unsupported performance claims.
entries.summary: Distinctive interface design, design themes, responsive audits and avoiding generic AI-looking layouts.

entries.name: AI Design Skills (Elaya)
entries.use_when: Planning a landing page from the audience and conversion goal, choosing a visual system, or producing motion demonstrations of an existing design.
look_for: Landing-page-design: offer, audience, structure, conversion copy and visual rules
Design-to-motion: animated showcase from a static design; inspect current prerequisites upstream
Editable design values and explicit design constraints
cautions: Read the specific upstream SKILL.md and its license/credits before using or adapting; some ideas reference additional upstream projects.
Do not invent conversion statistics, logos, testimonials or other proof.
A collection link is not evidence that its skills have been installed or tested in this project.
entries.summary: Landing-page content and visual systems, plus animation/motion showcase workflows.

entries.name: Aspire
entries.summary: Code-first app composition, service integrations, observability and local development for distributed apps.
entries.use_when: Working on .NET or mixed-language distributed systems; debugging services, telemetry and local app orchestration.
look_for: Official code-first app host and dashboard
Local orchestration and service integration patterns
OpenTelemetry and developer observability workflows
cautions: This is a developer platform, not an Agent Skill.
Check supported versions and required runtimes before adoption.
External services and deployments need explicit authorization.

entries.name: Microsoft Agent Framework
entries.summary: Build, orchestrate and host AI agents in .NET and Python, with reusable workflow patterns.
entries.use_when: Building backend agents, durable workflows, MCP integrations or multi-agent orchestration in .NET or Python.
look_for: Official agent orchestration and hosting examples
Agent Skills and MCP integration samples
Workflows, tool approval, observability and evaluation patterns
cautions: Framework integration is not equivalent to installing an Agent Skill.
Choose a current version and review runtime, provider and hosting requirements.
Use test credentials and explicit approvals for external model or service calls.

entries.name: oasdiff
entries.summary: Compare OpenAPI specifications and surface breaking changes in local tooling or CI.
entries.use_when: Reviewing backend API changes, migrating consumers, auditing schema changes and adding compatibility checks to pull requests.
look_for: Breaking-change rule catalog and accurate API diff semantics
PR review and CI integration patterns
Support for varied OpenAPI versions and schema compositions
cautions: Use trusted local specs; hosted side-by-side features may upload or share contract details.
License is Apache-2.0, not MIT; retain applicable notices if importing material.

entries.name: Playwright MCP
entries.summary: Give agents real browser navigation and interaction through a structured MCP interface.
entries.use_when: An agent needs to inspect a safe local app, reproduce a user journey, or gather actual interactive browser evidence.
look_for: Browser state lifecycle and isolated test sessions
Accessibility snapshots and deterministic page interaction
Agent client setup and permissions
cautions: An MCP connection alone is not proof that a browser workflow succeeded.
Use local/staging environments; avoid customer accounts or live payments.
Upstream also recommends Playwright CLI+Skills for some token-sensitive coding workflows.

entries.name: Playwright CLI
entries.summary: Run browser actions and inspect pages from a CLI; useful with coding-agent skill workflows.
entries.use_when: An agent or developer prefers concise shell-driven browser checks, screenshots, selector inspection or test reproduction.
look_for: Browser CLI commands and skills integration
Browser screenshots and element inspection
Tradeoffs versus a persistent MCP browser session
cautions: CLI automation is not a substitute for a safe test environment.
Verify client setup and isolation before testing live user journeys.
Do not execute upstream install scripts automatically just because this link is bookmarked.

entries.name: Superpowers
entries.summary: Composable agent workflows for planning, test-driven work, debugging and verification.
entries.use_when: Reviewing plans, implementing changes with evidence, debugging systematically, or creating a repeatable test-first agent workflow.
look_for: Verification-before-completion and clean evidence boundaries
Structured TDD and systematic debugging skills
Composable planning/review workflow, with realistic agent constraints
cautions: Strong opinionated workflows may conflict with a project's agreed process.
Check what commands and subagents a particular host actually supports.
Do not reproduce its skill instructions without following the MIT license conditions.

entries.name: Spec Kit
entries.summary: Structured specification, feature planning, bug investigation and decision reviews for coding agents.
entries.use_when: Starting a complex feature, reviewing ambiguous requirements or creating a traceable plan and decision record before implementation.
look_for: Spec-driven feature process and review checkpoints
Bugfix and idea assessment workflows
Documented outcomes and repeatable templates
cautions: Templates guide decisions but do not replace human review.
An entire process toolkit may be excessive for simple one-line tasks.
Verify tool and project integration requirements before introducing it.
